Decision summary

01 / Read first
Start with five courses that test both campuses, short workshops and deeper skills training.

Launch Knife Skills, Cookie & Biscuit Baking, Thai Street Food, Artisan Sourdough and Vegetarian & Vegan Cuisine. These cover accessible first purchases and multi-session commitment without opening the entire catalogue at once. Prices and schedules come from the proposed catalogue. [1]

Fees per session are derived by dividing the total fee by scheduled weeks; students still buy the full course. All linked market pages were checked on 24 September 2026 unless their own publication date is shown.

Who is likely to buy

02 / Personas
Practical learner

The home cook

Wants confidence with useful techniques and meals that can be repeated at home. Evening and weekend slots lower the scheduling hurdle.

Best fit: Knife Skills, Thai Street Food, Chinese Wok, Healthy Meal Prep. Commune and Palate Sensations market hands-on classes to beginners and home cooks. [4] [2]

Progression buyer

The committed hobby baker

Values coaching, technique and a path from basics to more complex bread, pastry and decoration.

Best fit: Bread Fundamentals, Sourdough, French Pastry, Macarons. ABC sells multi-lesson bread and cake courses; Creative Culinaire offers intensive hands-on baking. [5] [6]

Experience buyer

The social or gift buyer

Seeks a contained activity with something to take home. Some may attend with a friend, partner or family member.

Best fit: Cookie & Biscuit, Cupcake & Cake Pops, Knife Skills. Competitors list one-off sessions, family formats and gift vouchers. The size of this segment is UNKNOWN. [3] [2]

Demand and seasonality

05 / Evidence, with limits
Visible bookings

Commune Kitchen labels an upcoming dumpling class “only a few left”; Creative Culinaire marks its intensive cake and bread course fully booked. These are individual listing signals observed 24 Sep 2026, not a market fill-rate estimate. [4] [6]

16.9m visitors

Singapore’s 2025 international arrivals, up 2.3% on 2024, according to STB’s 3 Feb 2026 release. Food Playground sells local cultural cooking, but the share likely to buy this catalogue is UNKNOWN. [8] [7]

21 Nov–31 Dec

Singapore’s 2026 year-end school holiday. Food Playground advertises holiday cooking camps; ABC warns of longer lesson waiting lists in peak seasons such as December. This supports planning accessible year-end workshops, but the uplift for Cook & Bake is UNKNOWN. [9] [10] [5]

Festive rotation

ToTT’s calendar includes themed cupcakes and pineapple tarts alongside regular classes. Test seasonal versions of existing workshops; do not assume stable year-round demand for a festive recipe. Sales uplift is UNKNOWN. [3]

Launch these five first

06 / Recommended sequence

Knife Skills & Kitchen Essentials

CUL-210 · Bukit Timah · S$160 · 1 session

The lowest proposed upfront fee is a practical first purchase and a gateway to longer cooking courses. Test how many first-time students return. [1]

Cookie & Biscuit Baking

BAK-108 · Orchard Road · S$180 · 1 session

A giftable take-home workshop within the reference band; useful for a year-end seasonal variation. [1] [3]

Thai Street Food Cooking

CUL-202 · Bukit Timah · S$540 · 3 sessions · S$180/session

Commune’s S$185 single Thai class gives a direct offer to compare against Cook & Bake’s deeper three-session format. [1] [4]

Artisan Sourdough Bread Baking

BAK-101 · Orchard Road · S$680 · 4 sessions · S$170/session

Tests willingness to commit to specialist baking. ToTT and Creative Culinaire publish competing bread instruction. [1] [3] [6]

Vegetarian & Vegan Cuisine

CUL-208 · Bukit Timah · S$540 · 3 sessions · S$180/session

Tests a differentiated cooking theme already visible in Palate Sensations’ vegan offer and Commune’s plant-forward positioning. [1] [2] [4]

Risks to resolve

07 / Before scaling

Premium fees need a reason

The proposed Cupcake & Cake Pops workshop is S$220 for one session and Sushi & Sashimi is S$245 per session, above the reference band. Show what additional technique, materials or individual coaching earns that premium. Fee comparison ↑

Evidence is supply-side

Published listings and isolated booking labels show offers and some activity. Market-wide paid enrolments, conversion, fill rates and margins remain UNKNOWN. Track these in the first intakes before expanding.

Audience mismatch

Tourism and school-holiday activity are visible, but this catalogue has no Singapore heritage course or dedicated children’s programme. Treat those segments as future tests rather than forecast revenue. Demand evidence ↑
